item.title: Esports Heat up Boston: RLCS brings world’s best to Agganis Arena
item.description: If you walked past FitRec or Agganis Arena this weekend, you might have done a double-take at the bizarre, bug-eyed car sitting between the buildings.

item.title: MBTA reopens South Station overnight to homeless people during recent blizzard, City Council calls for further action
item.description: South Station was reopened to homeless people during the recent record-breaking blizzard, amid ongoing calls from Boston’s City Council for the city and the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority to adopt compassionate cold-weather emergency shelter policies. This winter, amid the Jan. 25 snowstorm and consistent sub-freezing temperatures, private security guards forced homeless people to leave South...

item.title: Records broken as hot start lifts BU men’s basketball to victory over Holy Cross
item.description: The Boston University men’s basketball team made history twice as they cruised past College of the Holy Cross for a 78-63 triumph on Wednesday at Case Gym — junior guard Michael McNair broke the program record for three-pointers in a season, and Joe Jones became the winningest head coach in BU men’s basketball history.

item.title: BU President Gilliam announces new ‘strategic framework’ for University priorities
item.description: Boston University President Melissa Gilliam issued a press release Wednesday announcing BU’s new strategic framework, which she called “Charting Our Future.” The framework includes a set of shared goals, guiding principles and initial programs which will align the BU community in a “common purpose to advance” the University.

item.title: ‘Links in a chain’: BU School of Law hosts ‘ICE Out’ training event to help activists support immigrant communities
item.description: The Boston University chapter of the American Association of University Professors held an “ICE Out Convening” and training event at the BU School of Law on Wednesday, where a group of law professors discussed how U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has impacted people in Massachusetts, and taught residents to know and exercise their rights.

item.title: I’m good at being embarrassing | Thought Daughters
item.description: Whether it’s through my terrible singing, even more terrible dance moves, hiring frat pledges to publicly wish my friend a happy birthday or even dressing up as a lobster for BU’s annual Lobster Night — I’m not joking about that, by the way. You can look it up — I’m going to keep putting myself out there, no matter how ridiculous I may look. If anyone’s wondering what I’m doing right now, chances are it’s something embarrassing.

item.title: The best — and worst — exercise classes across Boston
item.description: As someone who’s lived in the Boston area for my entire life, I’ve tried many local group fitness classes through ClassPass, a subscription that allows you to sign up for exercise classes at partner-studios worldwide. Personally, I look for an exhilarating workout that leaves me sore — in a good way, of course — and welcoming staff, as I believe this can make or break a workout experience. Here’s my critique on each of the studios I’ve tried.

item.title: Staying healthy during the winter: lessons in tea, sleep and stress relief
item.description: As winter intensifies, shorter days, colder temperatures and academic pressures can make staying healthy more difficult for many students. Informal wellness events hosted by Boston University Student Wellbeing, such as “Stress ReLeaf: Working with Tea for Calm and Focus,” a tea making event that aims to teach students mindfulness and give students opportunities to explore stress relief practices in a low-pressure environment.

item.description: Boston University, The Islamic Society of BU and Marsh Chapel have partnered for Ramadan to maintain spaces on campus for prayer and to provide Suhoor and Iftar meals for students who choose to fast in honor of the holy month.
